sections.heading: From biological understanding to engineered solutions
paragraphs: System Biology helps examine biological processes as interacting systems, while Synthetic Biology uses engineering-oriented design to modify or construct biological functions. Their combination can support healthcare, agriculture, industrial biotechnology and sustainable development.

sections.heading: Why ESTIC 2026 matters for policy analysis
paragraphs: The ESTIC 2026 platform is intended to bring scientists, policymakers, industry leaders, researchers and deep-tech innovators together across thematic areas including System and Synthetic Biology.

advisory_notes: “System Biology” should preferably be written as “Systems Biology” in the definitions and explanations.
The source supports ESTIC’s platform and intended role, but claims that it will improve translation or strengthen the ecosystem are analytical projections, not established outcomes.

The AI, biomanufacturing, biodesign, biosafety, biosecurity, ethics, access and regulatory-governance points are useful analysis, but should remain clearly distinguished from source-reported event facts.
The COVID-19 vaccine reference is presented in the source as an example of research leading to innovation; it should not imply that System or Synthetic Biology produced those vaccines.
The proposed answer-use line is truncated after “accessible” and should be completed before publication.
“Responsible innovation” is a valid analytical framing, but the supplied event text does not report specific responsible-innovation measures.

GS3.6 and GS3.1 are defensible internal syllabus tags for biotechnology and science-and-technology applications; GS2.6 is only defensible if the note explicitly develops governance, regulation, ethics or access dimensions.
The hypothetical production-method example is appropriately labelled, but its laboratory-to-industry pathway should not be read as evidence that such a project actually occurred.
